title: Volume permissions of empty volumes not persisted
body:
### Issue Description

Ownership and permissions changes of empty container volumes are not persisted between container restarts.

They are persisted in docker.
They are persisted for non-empty volumes.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
$ podman run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest chown 1000:1000 /vol
$ podman run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest ls -la /vol
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 root     root          4096 Dec  8 00:00 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 root     root          4096 Dec  8 00:00 ..
```

```
$ podman run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest sh -c 'touch /vol/testfile && chown 1000:1000 /vol'
$ podman run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest ls -la /vol
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 1000     1000          4096 Dec  8 00:00 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 root     root          4096 Dec  8 00:00 ..
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root             0 Dec  8 00:00 testfile
```

```
$ docker run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest chown 1000:1000 /vol
$ docker run --rm -it -v myvol:/vol alpine:latest ls -la /vol
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 1000     1000          4096 Dec  8 00:00 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 root     root          4096 Dec  8 00:00 ..
```

### Describe the results you received

Ownership not persisted

### Describe the results you expected

Ownership persisted

comments.body: Current behavior is a result of https://github.com/containers/podman/pull/22727 which was based on matching our behavior against Docker. Possible we missed a case and a deliberate chown of the mountpoint should also cause a stop in subsequent ownership change?
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.

I also have this issue. As a workaround, I currently **create a file named `.podmankeep`** in the volumes where I want to `chown` the root directory:

```
$ podman volume create myvol
myvol
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'chown -v 1000:1000 /v; touch /v/.podmankeep'
changed ownership of '/v' to 1000:1000
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'ls -la /v'
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 1000     1000          4096 Sep 21 09:59 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 root     root          4096 Sep 21 10:03 ..
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root             0 Sep 21 10:03 .podmankeep
```

I think this one is somewhat tied to our decision to, by default, mount named volumes as owned by the UID/GID the container is running as, not root (as Docker does). This makes it very difficult to identify when a deliberate chown by the user has taken place. We'd have to store original UID/GID for each volume and check it when the container finished.

At this point, I'm leaning towards adding a config field - `StrictDockerCompat` or similar - in `containers.conf`. Default it to false, current behavior. When set to true, we match Docker mount behavior as closely as possible - volumes owned by root by default, any chown is preserved, etc. This will also encourage us to start documenting exact differences between Docker and Podman somewhere.

@mheon thank you for the additional details :slightly_smiling_face:

A tiny addition from my side: I performed another experiment and I also noticed that, once a file is created inside the volume, the `chown` is always preserved from that point onwards, **even if the file is later removed**:

```
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'chown -v 1000:1000 /v; touch /v/.podmankeep'
changed ownership of '/v' to 1000:1000
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'ls -lan /v'
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 1000     1000          4096 Sep 22 21:15 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 0        0             4096 Sep 22 21:15 ..
-rw-r--r--    1 0        0                0 Sep 22 21:15 .podmankeep
$ ls -lan ~/.local/share/containers/storage/volumes/myvol/_data/
total 8
drwxr-xr-x 2 100999 100999 4096 Sep 22 21:15 .
drwx------ 3   1000   1000 4096 Sep 22 21:15 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1   1000   1000    0 Sep 22 21:15 .podmankeep
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'rm -v /v/.podmankeep'
removed '/v/.podmankeep'
$ podman run --rm -v myvol:/v docker.io/library/busybox sh -ec 'ls -lan /v'
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 1000     1000          4096 Sep 22 21:15 .
dr-xr-xr-x    1 0        0             4096 Sep 22 21:16 ..
$ ls -lan ~/.local/share/containers/storage/volumes/myvol/_data/
total 8
drwxr-xr-x 2 100999 100999 4096 Sep 22 21:15 .
drwx------ 3   1000   1000 4096 Sep 22 21:15 ..
```

I guess, once Podman detects the volume has something in it (at container termination), it is permanently marked as "not empty" somehow.

I hope this info is useful in some way :) Just in case, this is my `podman version` output (I'm on Debian Sid / Unstable):

```
$ podman version
Client:        Podman Engine
Version:       5.8.6
API Version:   5.8.6
Go Version:    go1.26.7
Built:         Wed Aug 26 23:11:23 2026
Build Origin:  Debian
OS/Arch:       linux/amd64
```

Yes. To be clear about the current behavior: each volume has a field called NeedsChown in the database. That starts off set to true, and when it's true, we perform a chown when we mount the volume into a container. It gets set to false if the volume is not empty when the container starts or if we chown to root:root (I don't really know why the last one is there...). So all you need is a single file in the volume at one point to unset the flag.

(We could probably allow this to be configured by `podman volume create --opt` as well, if we really wanted to, disable chowning to a different UID/GID entirely at volume creation).

> allow this to be configured by `podman volume create --opt` ... disable chowning to a different UID/GID entirely at volume creation

Actually this sounds like the perfect solution to me! An option to set the `NeedsChown` database field to `false` from the beginning. Just my personal opinion tho :)
